_about: Describes every Amass configuration setting so the AI config assistant can explain settings and propose changes grounded in the schema, not in hardcoded prose. Paths use dots: scope.domains, options.database. The transformations.* and datasources.* entries describe the per-item fields of a FROM->TO transformation and of a data source. A test fails when a config struct field or documented option has no entry here, so add an entry when a field is added. Nothing here enables collection or names a specific target; it only describes the schema.

sections.seed: Where an enumeration starts: the existing knowledge about the target (its domains, known names, address space, or company). The one section you really need; every seed entry is also in scope.
sections.scope: The boundary a discovered asset must fall within to be kept. Unless the run is -rigid, the engine may widen it as evidence appears, so it is a starting boundary, not a hard cap.
sections.options: Operational settings: the database, the engine, DNS resolvers, brute-force and alteration wordlists, active-probe pacing, and the default transform values.
sections.transformations: Which Open Asset Model asset-type transitions the engine collects, and each one's TTL, confidence, priority and excluded data sources. A key is FROM->TO, where TO is an asset type, ALL (every transition from that type), NONE (collect nothing from that type), or a data source name.
sections.datasources: The external data sources and their per-source credentials and TTLs, kept in the datasources.yaml file named by options.datasources.
sections.ai: Optional model, classifier and attribution settings. Advisory only; it never turns AI on by itself.

active.description: Whether active collection is allowed: zone transfers, certificate name grabs and service probes that contact the target directly. Passive collection is the default. The -active command-line flag sets it.

rigid_boundaries.description: When true, the scope never expands: only assets inside the configured scope are kept. When false, the engine may add assets it finds strong evidence belong to the target. The -rigid flag sets it.

scope.domains.description: Registered domains allowed in scope. A name is in scope when it is one of these or a subdomain of one.

scope.ips.type: list of IP addresses and ranges
scope.ips.description: IP addresses allowed in scope. Single addresses, dash ranges (192.0.2.3-8) and full ranges (192.0.2.10-192.0.2.20) are accepted.

scope.cidrs.description: CIDR ranges allowed in scope; an address inside one is in scope.

scope.asns.description: Autonomous system numbers allowed in scope; the networks they announce are in scope.

scope.organizations.description: Organizations (corporations) discovered assets must be attributable to. In the seed, a starting point the engine resolves to the company's domains, networks and systems.

scope.ports.description: Ports active enumeration may probe on in-scope addresses. Omit to probe every port the probes know; list ports only to narrow that. Ranges such as 8000-8010 work.

scope.blacklist.description: Subdomains that will never be investigated, even when otherwise in scope.

scope.names.description: Seed only. Known DNS names (leads), usually subdomains of an in-scope domain, supplied so the enumeration does not overlook them. Each lead's registered domain is added to the scope. The -nf flag adds names the same way.

scope.names_file.description: Seed only. A file of seed DNS names, one per line; its names are treated as leads like seed.names.

options.datasources.description: Path to the datasources.yaml file holding data source credentials and TTLs.

options.database.default: a local SQLite database under the output directory
options.database.description: The asset database connection string. PostgreSQL (postgres://...) and Neo4j (neo4j://... or bolt://...) are supported; without this a local SQLite database is used.

options.engine.default: http://127.0.0.1:4000 (a local engine is started when none is given)
options.engine.description: URL of the collection engine the client connects to.

options.resolvers.description: Untrusted DNS resolvers used for name resolution.

options.bruteforce.description: DNS brute forcing: enabled on/off and the wordlist files it uses.

options.alterations.description: Name alteration generation: enabled on/off and the wordlist files it uses.

options.default_transform_values.description: Defaults applied to a transformation that does not set its own ttl, confidence or priority.

options.minimum_ttl.description: The smallest TTL applied to data source responses; a source's shorter TTL is raised to this.

options.probe_pace_ms.description: Minimum spacing between active probes to one host, so a host is not reached by a burst across ports. 0 turns pacing off. Only hosts you control should be probed without pacing.

options.probe_jitter_ms.description: Additional random spread added to the probe pace, so a host's probes do not arrive on a fixed rhythm.

options.probe_timeout_ms.description: How long an active probe waits to connect to a host's port before giving up. Ports are probed one at a time per host, so a filtered or dead port waits out this whole duration; this is the main lever on how long active enumeration takes against unresponsive hosts. 0 or less uses the default.

transformations.ttl.description: How long a FROM->TO result is reused before it is collected again. A larger value re-collects less often.

transformations.confidence.description: The minimum confidence a result of this transition needs to be kept.

transformations.priority.description: The relative order in which this transition runs; lower runs sooner.

transformations.exclude.description: Data sources not to use for this transition, when the rest are still wanted.

datasources.name.description: The data source the entry configures, matching a source Amass knows.

datasources.ttl.description: How long this source's responses are reused before the source is queried again.

datasources.creds.type: object of named credential sets {username, password, apikey, secret}
datasources.creds.description: The source's credentials. Secrets are entered by the operator, never by a model.
